description:
Read-only set accessors clone the whole set on every lookup. Evidence (develop @ cca160808): - src/compiler2/deps.rs:125 output_keys -> OrderedSet, :173 waits_for -> HashSet>, :227 derivations_of -> OrderedSet

; each is `.get(..).cloned().unwrap_or_default()`. Callers that then copy the copy: scheduler.rs:497, :680, :683 (`output_keys(..).iter().cloned()`). ~25 call sites in scheduler.rs, drive.rs and world.rs. - src/compiler2/jobs/runtime_demand.rs:683-693 direct_surfaces, first_class_surfaces, direct_targets -> owned BTreeSet per lookup; the callers at :1063, :1064, :1079 only read. - src/compiler2/pull/rooted.rs:397, :418, :433, :589 `self.rooted_readers.get(member).cloned().unwrap_or_default()` before mutating `self.rooted`. Different fields of one struct; edition 2024 closures capture disjoint fields. :418 is field access only. - src/compiler2/pull.rs:1343 `self.fact_readers.get(fact_key).cloned()`. Change: the accessors return a borrow (an iterator or Option<&Set>); a caller that mutates the owner while holding the set clones at its own call site (scheduler.rs:637 `previously_owned` is a likely one). Method: per the epic strategy -- signature first, cargo check enumerates. Informed by .1's appeasement / interleaving ratio. Removal ledger: the `.cloned().unwrap_or_default()` in each accessor and every double clone at the callers. Signal: gate green, no golden/census/pin movement. Wake and emission order must not move: OrderedSet iteration order is what dependents wake in.
title: Set accessors on deps, callable flows and rooted readers return borrows
